newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Debt market unwinds, EMU strategies noted.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Debt market unwinds, EMU strategies noted.

text.p: Position-squaring was the order of the day in the European bond options market on Wednesday as it prepared for the dormant holiday period.

Dealers said there was barely any volume in exchange trade although they said strategies based on European yield convergence were still being touted. The over the counter market is all but closed as well, specialists say.
"There's no real initiation of flows," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in London. "I've had no customers wanting to put on trades. They're just unwinding postions they've had from before."
But he said convergence trades were "still flavour of the month", noting that if anything, people have been buying calls on Eurolire and BTPs.
Implied volatility levels for March Bund futures on LIFFE were broadly steady, trading around 5.75/90 percent at the money, after finishing at 5.89 percent on Tuesday.
Volatilities shot higher last week, rising to as high as 7.0 percent from around 5.5 percent, amid U.S.-led turbulence in bond and stock markets.
Enthusiasm for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) was regenerated over the weekend after European leaders agreed on a budget discipline accord and unveiled designs for new euro notes.

But a dealer at a British bank in London said that even if EMU was a theme for the markets, there was no evidence of players taking positions this close to the holidays. "It's very sparse to say the least."
He said that apart from a few muted sessions next week, the market would not get up and running again until the new year.
